Formulation
Patient presents with an acute, first-time, unilateral throbbing headache without associated red-flag neurological or systemic symptoms. No documented mental health issues; psychosocial factors appear stable. Predisposing: family history of migraine. Precipitating: not identified. Perpetuating: pain interfering with work and daily functioning. Protective: partner support.

Mental Health Care Plan Details

Principal Problem: New-onset headache interfering with daily functioning
- Patient Goal(s): Obtain pain relief; resume normal work activities
- Clinical Goal(s): Achieve headache control; monitor for escalation or red-flag symptoms; assess need for further investigation if persistent
- Actions (Patient):
  • Take prescribed stronger NSAID with food as directed  
  • May take Paracetamol concomitantly (per GP advice)  
  • Maintain hydration, rest, monitor symptoms; seek review if worsening, persists >48 h, or red-flag symptoms develop (fever, rash, vomiting, neck stiffness)
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  • Provide prescription for stronger NSAID; advise on combined use with Paracetamol  
  • Educate on red-flag symptoms and when to re-consult  
  • Arrange follow-up if headache persists or worsens; consider BP measurement and migraine evaluation if recurrent

Secondary Problem (if applicable):
- Not recorded

Patient Education, Emergency Care & Relapse Prevention
- Education Given: Yes. Topics Covered: Medication use, hydration, rest, red-flag symptoms (fever, rash, vomiting, neck stiffness), when to seek further care
- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening: Increased pain intensity, new neurological symptoms, systemic signs (fever, rash), persistent headache >48 h
- Coping Strategies: Rest, adequate fluid intake, regular analgesia as directed
